span.label: THE AMBIGUITY CONDITION, FOR THE FOURTH TIME AND FROM A FOURTH DIRECTION: `Quotation withheld WHEN THE IMPLICATIONS OF THIS INFORMATION ARE RELATIVELY AMBIGUOUS.` With higgins1977 (`at least in ambiguous situations`), north1999 (`only when there is an element of UNCERTAINTY`) and money2013 (`a situation that does not leave much room for interpretation`), **that is four papers across 1977-2015 and three fields.** And here it is not a qualifier in passing: it is one of four summarised findings, and the target behaviours were SELECTED for ambiguity by a separate rating study of 43 subjects before the experiment began
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: FREQUENCY IS A DOSE, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO AS A GENERAL LAW RATHER THAN A RESULT: `Quotation withheld.` Not `in this experiment` - in the past. **The claim is that ordinary life is continuously setting accessibility**, and the laboratory manipulation is only a controlled instance of something always running. That is a much larger claim than the experiment tests, and it is the one the field inherited
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE DECAY IS SLOW AND INCOMPLETE: `although these effects decrease with the time interval between their activation and the acquisition of information to be interpreted or encoded, they are SOMETIMES DETECTABLE EVEN AFTER 24 HOURS.` A priming effect surviving a day, in a corpus whose other records measure the same word in MILLISECONDS - vorberg2003's time courses, Holcomb2005's 40 ms primes, Huang2018's 16 ms exposure. **The same term spans six orders of magnitude of persistence**, and `sometimes detectable` is the hedge that keeps this one honest
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A GRADIENT USED TO RULE OUT A RIVAL ACCOUNT: the priming generalised to traits related to the primed one only indirectly, but LESS strongly - `Quotation withheld produced by exposure to `good` or `bad` concepts on the priming task.` **A halo would not respect the distance between traits.** The rival is excluded by the SHAPE of the effect rather than by a control condition, which is a cheaper and less common move
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THEY BORROW higgins1977'S MECHANISM EVIDENCE AND MARK THE BORROWING: `Quotation withheld ... Quotation withheld` They lean on Higgins' applicability null - primed traits that were evaluatively toned but INAPPLICABLE had no effect - for the mechanism their own design does not test, name it as a borrowing, and mark the inference tentative in the same paragraph. **Both papers are in this corpus and the dependency is now recorded from the borrowing side**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **THE `WHEN ... AMBIGUOUS` CLAUSE IS INSIDE THE QUOTE AND IT IS HALF THE CLAIM.** An edge reading `accessibility drives encoding` without it states the 1977-79 result as the unconditional version the field later argued about - and this is the fourth paper in the corpus to name that same condition. Weight 0.9: the paper's own summary of its own finding, in its discussion.
